frame: For the ISS cabin scenario, the oxygen and pressure recorded for each test are compared with the team bins (oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa); the bins are the team's choice. A test whose table holds no pressure value, or no oxygen value, is reported apart and is never placed inside a bin. The scenario also sets a flow range (5 to 30 cm/s); the flow speed of the matched tests is compared with it and does not change the counts. A test is counted for a need only if its investigation's PSI record states that need as an objective (objective sentences are linked to needs by the team pipeline). Inverse-flame tests, whose oxygen value is the burner stream (the gas issuing from the burner, not the surrounding atmosphere), are never matched to a crew atmosphere. Computed by the team's code from NASA PSI tables (code written with an AI assistant). Counts of recorded tests in the team's bins; not a statement about how a material behaves; not NASA's conclusion; not operational safety guidance.

needs.statement: Recorded tests (team count; team bins: oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa). 58 of the 136 tests counted for this need were recorded with oxygen inside the range of this environment; the experimental tables of these tests hold no pressure value. No counted test was recorded with oxygen and pressure both inside the ranges. The 58 by investigation: PSI-25 (BASS-II) 47, PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) 9, PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) 2. Pressure is not a column in the PSI experimental tables of PSI-25 (BASS-II), PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) and PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) (the PSI records of PSI-98 and PSI-99 say pressure was measured; the value is not in the table). All 58 are solid-material tests. Added carbon dioxide or helium is not a column in the PSI experimental tables of PSI-25 (BASS-II), PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) and PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II), so the balance gas of 58 tests is not in the table (the table of PSI-25 (BASS-II) has measured initial and final carbon dioxide readings, which the team pipeline does not read as added gas). Flow speed of the 58 tests with oxygen inside the range and pressure inside the range or not in the table: inside the flow range of this environment in 48 tests; not recorded in 1 test. The other 9 were recorded with a flow speed outside that range. What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test records the material, the oxygen at the start and at least one outcome: an event word, the difference between the initial and the final oxygen reading, a burn time or a burn length. The count is not a count of tests that burned, and the lowest oxygen tested is not a flammability limit.

Recorded tests (team count; team bins: oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa). No test in the mapped PSI tables is counted for this need: no test both records every required condition and at least one outcome variable of the need and comes from an investigation whose PSI record states the need as an objective. What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test would record the material, the oxygen and an ignition result. No mapped table records one for a solid fuel.

Recorded tests (team count; team bins: oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa). 11 of the 11 tests counted for this need were recorded with oxygen inside the range of this environment; the experimental tables of these tests hold no pressure value. No counted test was recorded with oxygen and pressure both inside the ranges. The 11 by investigation: PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) 9, PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) 2. Pressure is not a column in the PSI experimental tables of PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) and PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) (the PSI records of PSI-98 and PSI-99 say pressure was measured; the value is not in the table). All 11 are solid-material tests. Added carbon dioxide or helium is not a column in the PSI experimental tables of PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) and PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II), so the balance gas of 11 tests is not in the table. Flow speed of the 11 tests with oxygen inside the range and pressure inside the range or not in the table: inside the flow range of this environment in 11 tests; not recorded in 0 tests. What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test records the material, the flow speed and direction and a spread rate, burn length or burn time. Most counted tests record a length or a time and no spread rate; a burn time or a burn length is not a spread rate.

Recorded tests (team count; team bins: oxygen 19 to 23%, pressure 85.8 to below 116.8 kPa). 56 of the 299 tests counted for this need were recorded with oxygen and pressure both inside the ranges of this environment. All 56 come from PSI-69 (FLEX). A further 8 have recorded oxygen inside the bins and no pressure value the count can use (PSI-25 (BASS-II) 7, PSI-69 (FLEX) 1); pressure is not a column in the PSI experimental table of PSI-25 (BASS-II); the pressure cell of 1 test in the PSI experimental table of PSI-69 (FLEX) reads '0' (column 'Ambient pressure; mmHg'), which the team pipeline flags as out of range and does not use as a pressure. All 56 are fuel-droplet tests; none is a solid-material test. Of these 56, 27 have carbon dioxide or helium added to the atmosphere (20 carbon dioxide, 7 helium); the other 29 have recorded carbon dioxide and helium fractions of zero. Recorded test ends of these 56: 34 extinction, 17 disruption, 5 completion. 'Disruption' and 'extinction' are separate values of the table's 'Test end' column; a disruption is not read here as a flame extinction. Flow speed of the 64 tests with oxygen inside the range and pressure inside the range or not in the table: inside the flow range of this environment in 7 tests; not recorded in 57 tests. 272 further tests record the needed variables, but the investigation (PSI-159) does not state this need as an objective; they are not counted. These include inverse-flame tests, whose oxygen value is the burner stream and not an atmosphere. What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A counted test records the fuel, the oxygen and how the burn ended or an event word. In the FLEX table the ending is extinction, disruption or completion: the count is not a count of extinctions, and 'extinction' is also the recorded end of FLEX tests with no carbon dioxide and no helium added. The indicator 'S1.test_end' gives the count per ending.

What a count of this need means (the pipeline's reading): A test recorded for this need holds the material and the difference between the final and the initial CO or CO2 reading, or a mass loss rate. frame: For the Lunar base or pressurized rover scenario, the oxygen and pressure recorded for each test are compared with the team bins (oxygen 30 to 36%, pressure below 85.8 kPa); the bins are the team's choice. A test whose table holds no pressure value, or no oxygen value, is reported apart and is never placed inside a bin. The challenge statement names 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi (70.3 kPa) or less as the expected Moon Base atmosphere (CH.moonbase, read from a copy); the team's pressure bin is wider than that. No counted test was recorded at 30% oxygen or more and at or below 10.2 psi: the 17 counted tests inside the bins are fuel-droplet tests recorded at 30 to 34% oxygen and 71.2 to 72.4 kPa (about 0.7 atm), 1 to 2 kPa above it. A test is counted for a need only if its investigation's PSI record states that need as an objective (objective sentences are linked to needs by the team pipeline). Inverse-flame tests, whose oxygen value is the burner stream (the gas issuing from the burner, not the surrounding atmosphere), are never matched to a crew atmosphere. Every test in the PSI test tables is a microgravity test (gravity level set per table by the team from the PSI record); the tables hold no partial-gravity test, and microgravity and 1 g results are not shown here as bounds for lunar or Martian gravity. NASA's fire protection technical brief OCHMO-TB-008 says: "Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions." (TB008.gaps). Outside PSI, Table I of a paper on the NASA Technical Reports Server (Olson and Ferkul, NTRS-20130010991) gives limiting oxygen concentrations (the oxygen level below which the flame did not keep burning in the test) for three materials; for each of them, both limits at lunar gravity are lower than those at 1 g and at 0 g. These low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop-tower tests, and the paper says their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1 g; the table was read by an AI assistant and not checked by a person (OF2012.table1). Computed by the team's code from NASA PSI tables (code written with an AI assistant). Counts of recorded tests in the team's bins; not a statement about how a material behaves; not NASA's conclusion; not operational safety guidance.

frame: The pipeline sets no oxygen or pressure range for the Mars habitat scenario, so no recorded test is counted as matching its atmosphere. A test is counted for a need only if its investigation's PSI record states that need as an objective (objective sentences are linked to needs by the team pipeline). Every test in the PSI test tables is a microgravity test (gravity level set per table by the team from the PSI record); the tables hold no partial-gravity test, and microgravity and 1 g results are not shown here as bounds for lunar or Martian gravity. NASA's fire protection technical brief OCHMO-TB-008 says: "Material flammability in partial gravity remains a major gap for exploration missions." (TB008.gaps). Outside PSI, Table I of a paper on the NASA Technical Reports Server (Olson and Ferkul, NTRS-20130010991) gives limiting oxygen concentrations (the oxygen level below which the flame did not keep burning in the test) for three materials; for each of them, both limits at Martian gravity are lower than those at 1 g, and for some of them they are lower than those at 0 g as well. These low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop-tower tests, and the paper says their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1 g; the table was read by an AI assistant and not checked by a person (OF2012.table1). The scorer preset for this scenario sets no atmosphere. NASA's Exploration Atmospheres Working Group report lists 8.0 psia (55.2 kPa) and 7.6 psia (52.4 kPa), each with 32% oxygen, among its nominal atmospheres for surface habitats and says they are not requirements (EAWG.atmospheres); the kPa values are the team's conversion, and the preset does not use these atmospheres. Computed by the team's code from NASA PSI tables (code written with an AI assistant). Counts of recorded tests in the team's bins; not a statement about how a material behaves; not NASA's conclusion; not operational safety guidance.
